title: Open every implementation file with its component URN marker

facts.note: Bun/htmx implementation source and template extensions. Applies to every such file in scope, whether new, edited or pre-existing; not gated on operation, phase or a prior detector finding.
Test files and vendored/generated trees are excluded.

fires: Creating or editing a .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.mts implementation file without a leading `// URN: component:…` line
Creating or editing an .html/.htm template whose first meaningful line is not `<!-- URN: component:… -->`
An existing, untouched implementation file in scope that lacks the marker
An implementation file whose URN marker sits below the imports or other content
doesNotFire: Files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated
A file whose first meaningful line is the URN marker, preceded only by blank lines and an allowed shebang or HTML doctype

given: A Bun/htmx implementation file (.ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .mts, .html/.htm template) outside test files and vendored/generated trees
when: the file exists in scope (new, edited or pre-existing)
then: Its first meaningful line MUST be a `URN: component:…` marker — `// URN:` in source, `<!-- URN: … -->` in a template — after only blank lines and an allowed shebang or HTML doctype.
prefer: During GREEN: derive the URN from the plan ownership of the implementation being added.
During GREEN: use `//` syntax for code and `<!-- … -->` for templates.
During GREEN: add only the marker; don't restructure a correctly placed file.
avoid: Marker below imports or any content (reads as MISSING).
Inventing a wagon, feature, component, side, or layer.
Copying a nearby file's URN without verifying ownership.
Moving code merely to make the marker easier to write.
unless: Test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`): bound by their acceptance URNs instead.
A shebang or `<!doctype>` may precede the marker.
why: The URN is the only edge between a source file and the plan graph; without it no acceptance can claim the file, no wagon owns it, and coverage cannot see it exists.
evidence: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-URN-001 / BUN-GREEN-URN-MARKER-001 finding for in-scope implementation files.
The file is traceable from its real component URN (URN matches the plan ownership of the implementation).
verifier_detail: Scanned extensions: .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .mts and .html/.htm templates; skip *.test.*, *.spec.*, and node_modules, dist, build, _generated.
Dual-syntax detection: `// URN: component:…` in source, `<!-- URN: component:… -->` in templates.

Detector tolerance (not a coder permission): the header region is the leading run of blank lines, an optional shebang or doctype, and single-line comments; the first real content line ends it. A marker below the imports therefore reads as MISSING, which is the point.
first_meaningful_line: the first line that is neither blank nor a preamble; a shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env bun`) or `<!doctype>` is not content and must not displace the marker.
Unlike the Vite sibling (which counts a shebang as the first non-empty line and so reports a header it actually has as missing), this realization skips the shebang.

traceability_header: the leading comment block binding a file to the plan graph — URN, Tested-By, Runtime, Purpose; `//` in source, `<!-- … -->` in .html templates. This rule checks only the URN marker.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Aliases: GREEN-URN-001 (shared core alias, also carried by the Python realization and coder.vite.green-urn-marker), BUN-GREEN-URN-MARKER-001.

Stack-neutral obligation (required in every implementation file) with a Bun-specific dual-syntax detector. The Python realization writes `# URN:` and the Vite one `// URN:`; this is the same obligation with a third comment syntax.

Source fix_hint headings: 'Canonical path:' (its single item — URN on the first meaningful line after only an allowed shebang/doctype — is carried by then), 'During GREEN:' (scopes the ownership/syntax/add-only repair guidance, kept as a prefix in prefer[0..2]), 'Do not broaden:' (avoid[1..3]), 'Prove:' (evidence[1..2]).
Severity 3; disposition strict (atdd-bun fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline).

sharedNodes.text: strict: the extension fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Activation facts and fires/doesNotFire situations (including the explicit 'existing untouched file' example).
